raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add an optional token-span `chunk_size` to `BlockStored` so consumers can distinguish an independently retrievable GPU block from one offloaded chunk containing multiple advertised block hashes. This is a small, independently reviewable step toward #52103.

## Claims

- Native GPU events report the valid span of their retrievable block.
- Self-describing offload events report the full retrievable chunk span; partial tails report their valid span. Placeholder events leave the field unset.
- `block_size`, `block_hashes`, and `BlockRemoved` retain their existing meaning and behavior.

## Validation

- On GPU Server: `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py` — 60 passed.
- On GPU Server: `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k event` — 21 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files — passed.
- The human submitter confirmed line-by-line review and relevant test execution. No model evaluation is needed for this event-metadata-only change.

## Details

An offload `BlockStored` describes one retrievable chunk; its last block hash is the chunk key. Previously, `block_size` described each constituent block but did not tell consumers the span of the retrievable unit. This adds that span without collapsing the per-block hash list or repurposing `block_size`.

The field is optional so other event producers can leave it unspecified. Rich offload events populate it from the group chunk size (or the valid partial-tail span), and GPU events populate it from the emitted block span. Serialized placeholders omit it. The offload usage guide documents the contract, including that constituent offload hashes are not independently retrievable. Removal semantics are deliberately out of scope.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, and this PR description.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill.
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Adds one optional event field and populates it at existing event producers.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Covers GPU, full and partial offload chunks, placeholders, and wire serialization; related tests and pre-commit pass.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps existing block/removal behavior and documents the new field.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** States the contract, scope, limitations, and validation.

</details>

 | `spec_module_path` | no | — | both | Python import path for a custom `OffloadingSpec` not in the built-in registry. Required only when `spec_name` is not built-in (advanced). |
 | `canonical_layout` | no | `false` | both | Store each offloaded block in a common canonical representation instead of each worker's local GPU page (enables sharing across TP sizes and single-copy storage of replicated KV). See [Canonical Layout](#canonical-layout). |
 
+### KV event chunk size
+
+A `BlockStored` event advertises one retrievable unit. Native GPU events set
+`chunk_size` to `block_size` (or the valid span of a partial block).
+Self-describing offload events set it to the token span of the whole chunk,
+which may contain several `block_size` blocks. The constituent hashes are not
+independently retrievable from offload; the last hash in `block_hashes` identifies
+the chunk. Partial tails report their valid token span. Placeholder events leave
+`chunk_size` unset. This does not change `BlockRemoved` events.
+
 ## Canonical Layout
 
 By default, each worker copies its own GPU page to the CPU tier unchanged, so an offloaded block is stored in whatever form that worker happens to hold it.
